annotations.description: MiMo Stoic activated Myriad Landscape's sacrifice ability while Solemn Simulacrum is on the stack (being cast). The Myriad Landscape costs {2} + tap + sacrifice, which uses the 2 colorless mana from the Mountain and Plains (the only untapped lands), plus taps and sacrifices the Landscape itself. This means after Solemn Simulacrum resolves and fetches a land, MiMo will have lands but they'll all enter tapped. The issue is that Mind Stone is in hand and costs {2}. If MiMo had played the Study Hall from hand first (land drop), then tapped Mountain + Plains for {2} to cast Mind Stone, they would have had Mind Stone on the battlefield as a mana rock, while keeping Myriad Landscape for a future turn when they could better afford to sacrifice it (or sacrifice it next turn with more mana available). Sacrificing Myriad Landscape on turn 4 with Solemn Simulacrum already fetching a land means heavy investment in ramp this turn while deploying no artifacts for Osgir synergy. However, getting two basics is strong ramp, so this is debatable — but the sequencing of not playing Mind Stone first (using the 2 available mana) before committing to the Landscape activation seems suboptimal since Mind Stone could have been cast with the Mountain + Plains mana, and the Landscape sacrificed on a later turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Myriad Landscape's sacrifice ability to search for two basic lands, using all available mana while Solemn Simulacrum was on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Play Study Hall as land for turn, then tap Mountain + Plains to cast Mind Stone. Save Myriad Landscape activation for a future turn when the tempo cost is lower, since Solemn Simulacrum is already ramping this turn.

annotations.description: Fetched 2 Plains with Myriad Landscape when hand contains Thopter Engineer (2R), Hellkite Tyrant (4RR), and already has a Plains in hand. With only 1 Mountain on board, red mana is the bottleneck. Getting 2 Mountains would provide 3R+1W from lands, with the Plains in hand covering future white needs.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched 2 Plains from Myriad Landscape, resulting in 1 Mountain + 3 Plains
annotations.betterLine: Fetch 2 Mountains from Myriad Landscape to have 3 Mountains + 1 Plains, enabling Thopter Engineer immediately and progressing toward Hellkite Tyrant's RR requirement, while the Plains in hand covers white mana needs.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic sacrificed Mind Stone to draw a card on turn 4, but they have 6 cards in hand including Hellkite Tyrant (6 mana), Thopter Engineer (3 mana), and Key to the City (2 mana). With only 5 lands and Mind Stone, they had 6 mana sources. Sacrificing Mind Stone drops them to 5 mana sources, making it harder to cast Hellkite Tyrant on turn 5 (needs 6 mana including RR). They also have a land in hand (Plains or Mountain) they could play, but even with that they'd only have 6 lands next turn - exactly enough for Hellkite Tyrant if they kept Mind Stone. By sacrificing it, they now need to draw into another land or delay their biggest threat. The Mind Stone was more valuable as ramp toward the 6-mana Hellkite Tyrant than as a card draw at this stage.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Mind Stone to draw a card during postcombat main phase on turn 4.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Mind Stone for mana to cast Key to the City or Thopter Engineer instead, preserving Mind Stone as a mana source to enable casting Hellkite Tyrant on turn 5 with a land drop.
